{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mi-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"44357743f2a67bdbd28213d94ffe638df39397892f320ee5c786e16f59d3e3b4","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mi-class-std:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"7af7437894a2c63b20529c8a1ed7c10696796036051dd6666178ab579008ca37","source_liveness_sha256":"e81e5179580dc89fb25fdf5194e9f75291db3aa019fc21ccfe32c38d1a9df42f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Residency, licenses and REAL ID","heading":"C2 — Confusables and KG hints, residency, licenses and REAL ID","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, residency, licenses and REAL ID

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
The two conviction rules differ: a never-licensed applicant is refused at two or more moving-violation convictions in three years, while any applicant may carry at most one conviction in the three years before applying. [A01]
Why it matters: group licensing-eligibility; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F09, sec01-F10 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
An out-of-state license stays usable only until Michigan residency is established, and it is invalidated at the moment the Michigan application is accepted, not when the new card arrives. [A01]
Why it matters: group new-residents; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F04, sec01-F07 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A01
Vehicle title and registration must be done immediately by a new resident, whereas the driver’s license application waits until residency is established. [A01]
Why it matters: group new-residents; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F03, sec01-F04 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A02
The chauffeur’s license threshold is a vehicle rated 10,000 pounds GVWR driven mainly for work, while the commercial license threshold for a single vehicle is 26,001 pounds GVWR. [A02]
Why it matters: group license-types; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec01-F12, sec01-F13 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A02
Age 18 lets a commercial driver operate only inside Michigan, while age 21 is the line for crossing state lines or hauling placarded hazardous materials. [A02]
Why it matters: group license-types; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F14 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A02
A licensed driver needs no moped license at all, while an unlicensed teen needs to be at least 15, have parental approval, and pass vision, knowledge and sign tests. [A02]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F17, sec01-F18 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A02
The full CY endorsement covers motorcycles in general, while the CY 3W restriction limits the rider to three-wheeled motorcycles only. [A02]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F19, sec01-F20 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A02
Rider education is optional for most adults but mandatory for riders aged 16 to 17 and for adults after a second failed motorcycle skills test. [A02]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F19 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A03
An enhanced card without a star is already REAL ID compliant, while a standard card marked Not for Federal Identification is not, even though both remain valid for driving. [A03]
Why it matters: group real-id; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec01-F15, sec01-F25, sec01-F28 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A03
REAL ID adds no cost at renewal, but asking for it between renewals triggers the duplicate card fee. [A03]
Why it matters: group real-id; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F27 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A03
Licenses from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany or South Korea convert without testing, while an expired foreign license or an out-of-state license expired for at least four years sends you through a TIP and a skills test. [A03]
Why it matters: group new-residents; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec01-F31, sec01-F32 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A03
The Graduated Driver Licensing requirement for under-18 applicants is waived only when the teen has held a valid license from another state for more than a year. [A03]
Why it matters: group gdl; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F34 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]
